title: Inner-Product vs. Additive Masking Trade-Off
summary: Inner-product masking incurs substantial encoding overhead, and whether its low-noise security–efficiency trade-off beats simpler additive masking remains open.

formal_statement.body: For low-noise implementations, determine whether inner-product (IP) masking, despite the significant implementation overhead of computing on IP encodings, provides a more favorable security-versus-efficiency trade-off than the simpler multiplication algorithms used by additive masking schemes.

scope.domain: Side-channel cryptanalysis comparing inner-product and additive masking in low-noise implementations.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether inner-product masking offers a more favorable security-versus-efficiency trade-off than additive masking despite the overhead of computing on inner-product encodings.

citations.label: Effective and Efficient Masking with Low Noise using Small-Mersenne-Prime Ciphers

progress.summary: The source contrasts reported low-noise security gains from inner-product masking with significant encoding overhead. It explicitly leaves open whether the overall trade-off compares favorably with simpler additive-masking multiplication.
citation_labels: Loïc Masure et al., Effective and Efficient Masking with Low Noise using Small-Mersenne-Prime Ciphers
